page_title: UMST — every deadline and meeting, on your Mac desktop

sources.entry: UMST - Desktop calendar widget that brings together Google, iCloud, Outlook, Apple Reminders, Canvas and other LMS deadlines, Todoist, Asana and Trello, with menu bar quick add. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/nicoleyangcoding/UMST-UltimateMacSchedulingTool) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: UMST
summary.one_liner: UMST is a free, open-source native macOS desktop calendar widget that gathers deadlines and meetings from Canvas, Google, Outlook, Apple Reminders, Todoist and other services into one list on your desktop.
use_cases: see all school deadlines on the desktop
track Canvas assignments without opening a browser
combine work and personal calendars on a Mac
view Apple Reminders and Todoist tasks alongside meetings
hide windows to glance at the day's schedule
summary.what_it_does: UMST pulls events and deadlines from Canvas, Google Calendar, Gmail invites, iCloud, Outlook/Microsoft 365, Exchange, Yahoo, Apple Reminders, Todoist, Asana, Trello and any iCal link into a single list shown on the desktop behind other windows. Accounts already set up on the Mac are detected automatically; other sources are added by pasting a link. A Show Desktop feature (a separate menu bar app by @stanczykwyatt, installed by the install command) hides all windows with one click or the ⌃⇧D shortcut. Credentials and links are stored in the macOS Keychain, and the app has no account or analytics. It is written in native Swift for Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
notable: Native Swift app with Keychain-based token storage and no account or analytics
Show Desktop menu bar companion with ⌃⇧D shortcut
Connects many LMS platforms (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, Schoology, Google Classroom, D2L Brightspace) via calendar links
caveats: Not yet notarized by Apple; the .zip download requires approving it in System Settings → Privacy & Security
Show Desktop is a separate app; it can be skipped with SHOW_DESKTOP=0 in the install command
